lines.text: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews, setting an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar.
Haman son of Abihail cast the Pur to destroy the Jews, but his scheme came back on his head.
The days were called Purim, from the word Pur, and every generation was to remember and celebrate them.
Queen Esther and Mordecai confirmed the Purim letter, and Esther's decree confirmed the regulations, which were written into the record.
Mordecai's greatness was written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, and he was second only to the king.
